source.title: Tracking multiple items through occlusion: Clues to visual objecthood.

confidence_rationale: The most pointed paper in the pull for the memo's exact gap: it shows object tracking SURVIVES complete occlusion when the disappearance/reappearance carries accretion-deletion cues at an occluding contour, but BREAKS when items vanish in non-occlusion ways (imploding/exploding). This is direct evidence that token persistence is computed from spatiotemporal continuity cues, not from continuous visibility -- exactly the 'this object tracked through occlusion' capability MECH-045's object-file buffer must provide and REE's type-tag store cannot. Held at 0.77 (not higher) because it is human psychophysics and because it specifies WHICH cues license persistence rather than a mechanism REE can directly implement.
failure_signatures: Persistence is conditional on specific cues: tracking survives occlusion ONLY with accretion/deletion along a fixed occluding contour and breaks under implosion/explosion -- a REE object-file buffer that persists tokens unconditionally (e.g. on any temporary absence) would over-generalise beyond what the visual system actually does.
It diagnoses the CUES that signal enduring objecthood, not the buffer mechanism; REE still has to choose a representation that consumes continuity cues, which this paper does not supply.
Human visual psychophysics with abstract moving items; transfer to a latent-stack foraging agent whose 'occlusion' is a different sensory regime is non-trivial.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Across three experiments, multiple-object tracking was unimpaired when targets were briefly but completely occluded, PROVIDED the disappearance and reappearance carried accretion/deletion cues along fixed occluding contours; tracking was impaired when items disappeared and reappeared in non-occlusion ways (imploding/exploding into and out of existence) -- so the visual system computes enduring objecthood from spatiotemporal continuity cues, treating an occluded object as the SAME persisting token.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-045 asserts object-file-like buffers that 'bind features across time and motion' for minimal entity persistence. Scholl & Pylyshyn shows the strongest form of that persistence -- a token survives a total perceptual gap -- and pins down its trigger: continuity/occlusion cues, not continuous visibility. This is the precise 'this object tracked through occlusion' capability the object-representation memo flags as the token-vs-type gap: REE's live z_resource/z_object is a type tag that cannot track a particular instance across a gap, whereas this is exactly what an object-file buffer must do.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper specifies the perceptual CUES that license persistence (accretion/deletion at an occluding contour); it does not supply the buffer mechanism, and persistence is CONDITIONAL not automatic. REE must choose a representation that consumes continuity cues; persisting tokens unconditionally would over-read the result. Human-psychophysics-to-agent transfer applies.
mapping.source_context: Human visual psychophysics; multiple-object tracking with brief total occlusion vs non-occlusion (implosion/explosion) disappearances; 3 experiments.

confidence_components.notes: Directly targets the token-through-occlusion gap. High mapping fidelity to MECH-045's across-time/motion persistence clause; discounted because it characterises the triggering cues, not an implementable buffer, and persistence is cue-conditional.
